clue.text: Vendors of nameless material

indicators.note: read as making up the stuff of something, so these letters are the raw material reshaped into a new word

explanation.surface: Sellers of fabric that carries no brand or label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' looks like the cloth being sold, but it signals that the letters of NAMELESS are worked into another order.
explanation.definitionFit: Salesmen are people whose job is selling goods, which is what vendors do.

clue.text: Quiet about being involved in depressing broadcast

indicators.note: these pieces become involved in, that is set inside, the word for depressing

parts.note: sad can mean depressing, as in a sad state of affairs
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A muted remark about a gloomy radio programme.
explanation.definitionFit: To scatter seed or news widely is to spread it, the original farming sense of broadcast.

clue.text: Greek island raising a new variety of melons

indicators.note: a new variety reshapes the original, so the letters of the fruit are rearranged

explanation.surface: An Aegean isle grows a novel strain of melon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising a' just joins, though it reads as growing crops.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an island in the northern Aegean Sea.

clue.text: For a gentleman about 50 to tell a story is not so shrewd

indicators.note: the gentleman's title goes about, that is around, the other pieces

parts.note: Sir is the title for a knight or gentleman
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
to lie is to tell a story, a falsehood

explanation.surface: A gentleman of about fifty telling tales is less astute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' and 'is' link; the pieces go between the I and R of SIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Being less shrewd means being more foolish.

clue.text: Left behind the listening equipment? Lord!

indicators.note: in a down clue the letter for left goes behind, that is after, the other piece

parts.note: the ear is the body's listening equipment

explanation.surface: Someone forgot their headphones and exclaims in dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lord!' looks like an exclamation but is the definition, a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer of this rank is a British nobleman, addressed as Lord.

clue.text: Poor performer. setting lawyers back a little

indicators.note: setting something back here means the word for lawyers is read in the other direction

parts.note: the Bar is the collective name for barristers
a bit is a little

explanation.surface: An incompetent player puts the legal profession back a step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns BAR into RAB, and 'setting' just joins. In British sporting slang a rabbit is a weak player, especially a tail-end batsman at cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: British sporting slang uses the word for a hopeless player, typically a feeble batsman in cricket.

clue.text: A group of musicians on leave

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: A pop group is on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' looks like a noun, holiday, but is the verb, to desert.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert someone or something is to forsake it, walking away for good.

clue.text: Lawbreaker making great, start with a film

parts.note: big means great
a mist is a film, as of condensation

explanation.surface: A criminal's breakthrough began with a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' and 'start with' join; 'film' is a thin coating, not a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrying a second spouse while still married is a crime, so such a person breaks the law.

clue.text: Showing irascibility is sent up among sailors

indicators.note: something placed among others is set inside them, so the turned word goes within the sailors

parts.note: tars are sailors

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Being sent up among seamen shows bad temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads 'sent' from bottom to top before it goes among the sailors; 'Showing irascibility' stands for the quality itself, and 'is' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharpness of tone or manner shows a quick temper, so acerbity displays irascibility.

clue.text: People taking a walk in the rose-garden

definitions.text: People taking a walk in the rose-garden

parts.words: People taking a walk in the rose-garden
parts.note: a stroll among roses, but the word also names climbing roses that sprawl over garden walls

explanation.surface: Visitors strolling among the flower beds.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both country walkers and a kind of climbing rose, so the garden scene covers both senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Hikers who stroll for pleasure share their name with rambling roses that clamber across trellises.

clue.text: Hector is a beast!

definitions.meaning: to hector is to bully or pester someone
a burrowing, black-and-white striped animal of the weasel family

explanation.definitionFit: To pester someone persistently is to bully them, and the striped nocturnal mammal shares the word.

clue.text: He finds the Isle of Man capital!

definitions.text: He finds the Isle of Man capital!

parts.words: He finds the Isle of Man capital!
parts.note: a man who enjoys the island, but also a man's first name that is the island's chief town

explanation.surface: A man thinks the Manx island is splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like the old slang for excellent, but it is also the island's chief town, which shares the name with a man.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common man's first name and the chief town of the island in the Irish Sea.

clue.text: A handsome young man — a fellow one's to join

parts.note: a don is a fellow of an Oxford or Cambridge college
one is I, and the 's is S, as in 'one is'

explanation.surface: A good-looking youth is introduced to a college fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to join' simply links the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the youth loved by Aphrodite for his beauty gave his name to any strikingly good-looking lad.

clue.text: A servant named Ernie?

definitions.meaning: a man bound to serve, a serf or slave
ERNIE is the British machine that picks winning Premium Bond numbers, so whimsically a man of bonds

explanation.definitionFit: A bound serf is a man in bondage, and ERNIE, the Premium Bonds draw machine, is jokingly a man of bonds.

clue.text: A good man: growing old and putting on an act?

parts.note: St, saint, is a good man
aging means growing old

explanation.surface: A virtuous man getting on in years may be just pretending.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a play on putting on a theatrical performance, not pretending.
explanation.definitionFit: Mounting a production in the theatre is presenting a play on stage.

clue.text: Advocates a post-sorting reorganisation

indicators.note: a reorganisation reshuffles what is there, so these twelve letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Campaigners call for the mail-sorting office to be restructured.
explanation.definitionFit: Champions of a cause are its leading supporters, people who argue on its behalf.

clue.text: Collected and wrote notes

definitions.meaning: wrote music, as a composer does

explanation.definitionFit: A calm person is self-possessed, and a composer writing music has set down its notes.

clue.text: At one time a nanny user went free

indicators.note: letters set free are loosed from their order, so these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A childminder from the old days left a client and got off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At one time' marks the job as historical: a woman employed to breastfeed another's baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly a woman hired to suckle someone else's baby, the forerunner of a children's nurse.

clue.text: A subject of interest in the main

definitions.text: A subject of interest in the main

parts.words: A subject of interest in the main
parts.note: 'in the main' seems to mean 'mostly', but the main is the open sea, so this is a study of the sea

explanation.surface: A topic that is broadly interesting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old poetic word for the ocean, not the phrase 'on the whole'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the science studying the seas, and the main is literary language for the ocean.

clue.text: Celebrity needs no schedule.

parts.note: a table is a schedule, as in a timetable

explanation.surface: A famous person never needs an agenda.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known person is a VIP or dignitary, someone of note.

clue.text: Investment at the usual place.

parts.note: investment is an old word for clothing, and a habit is a monk's or nun's garment

explanation.surface: Putting money in at the same old spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investment' is not money but robing, being invested in garments.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal or plant's natural home is where it usually lives.

clue.text: To live in a city centre's ideal

indicators.note: the letters sit in the following words, running across 'centre's' and 'ideal'

explanation.surface: Living downtown is the perfect choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To live in a city' reads as the definition, but only 'To live' defines; 'in' points to the letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to make one's home there.

clue.text: Rate a fool over. a letter written

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece over another stands above it, so comes first

parts.note: an ass is a fool
ess is the letter S written out as a word

explanation.surface: Judge a fool for a letter he has written.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate something is to judge its worth, rating it.

clue.text: He regrets having to write it about'

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'He regrets having to write it about'', ends in a stray apostrophe and looks cut short: PEN + IT leaves ENT unaccounted for (probably 'about ten'), and no source gives the full text.
annotationWithheld.clue: He regrets having to write it about'

clue.text: Superior seaman presented to the old queen

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a rating in the navy
Bess is Queen Elizabeth I, Good Queen Bess

explanation.surface: A senior sailor is introduced to Elizabeth I.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superior' is the noun, as in Mother Superior, the head of a convent; 'presented to' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a convent of nuns is addressed as Mother Superior.

clue.text: Supported a wearying man

definitions.meaning: carried or held up, past tense

explanation.definitionFit: Carried a weight is the past tense of bear, and a tedious person tires others out.

clue.text: The way a dress appears in disco lighting

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
a robe is a long dress

explanation.surface: A frock looks different under the flashing club lights.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashing lamp giving rapid bursts of light is a fixture of dance floors.

clue.text: 23 across is not in favour of the routine

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
trite means hackneyed or routine

explanation.surface: A repentant person objects to everyday humdrum.
explanation.walkthrough: '23 across' is a cross-reference to another light meaning repentant; 'is' and 'of the' link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone sorry for wrongdoing and full of remorse.

clue.text: Animals holding a record can get more difficult to understand

indicators.note: one thing holding another has it inside, so the animals' word surrounds the record

parts.note: deer are animals
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Creatures clutching a disc become harder to fathom.
explanation.definitionFit: Profound thought is harder to grasp, as deep water is harder to see into.

clue.text: Worries about the birds' protection

indicators.note: one word goes about another when it surrounds it, so the worries enclose the next word

parts.note: fears are worries

explanation.surface: Anxieties about how birds are kept safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumage keeps birds warm and dry, shielding their bodies.
